definition: To turn off a computer, or to close a business.
exampleSentence: Always save your work before you shut down the computer.

definition: To start a computer and load its system.
exampleSentence: My old laptop takes five minutes to boot up in the morning.

definition: To connect a device to electricity.
exampleSentence: Remember to plug in your phone before you go to sleep.

definition: To move down a page on a screen.
exampleSentence: Scroll down to the bottom of the page to find the contact form.

definition: To make an image on a screen look bigger.
exampleSentence: You can zoom in on the map to see the street names.

definition: To make an image on a screen look smaller.
exampleSentence: Zoom out a little so we can see the whole city on the map.

definition: To make a paper copy of a document.
exampleSentence: Please print out the report and bring it to the meeting.

definition: To solve a problem or organize something.
exampleSentence: The IT team will sort out the problem with your email account.

definition: To start talking about a subject.
exampleSentence: I will bring up the budget issue at our next meeting.

definition: To do a task, test or plan.
exampleSentence: The scientists will carry out more tests next month.

definition: To take control of something.
exampleSentence: A larger company plans to take over our small startup.

definition: To give your work to a teacher or boss.
exampleSentence: Students must hand in their essays by Friday afternoon.

definition: To give something to each person in a group.
exampleSentence: The teacher will hand out the exam papers in five minutes.

definition: To investigate a problem.
exampleSentence: The support team promised to look into the payment error.

definition: To check or review something carefully.
exampleSentence: Let us go over the main points of the plan once more.

definition: To experience something hard, or to examine something.
exampleSentence: Many new companies go through a difficult first year.

definition: To write information in the spaces of a form.
exampleSentence: Please fill in your name and phone number on this card.

definition: To cancel a planned event.
exampleSentence: They had to call off the football match because of the snow.

definition: To build or create something from parts.
exampleSentence: It took us two hours to put together the new desk.

definition: To enter a place or system illegally.
exampleSentence: Hackers tried to break into the company network last night.

definition: To stop the supply of something.
exampleSentence: The storm may cut off electricity to thousands of homes.

definition: To give something for free.
exampleSentence: The shop will give away free coffee to the first fifty customers.

definition: To accept work, or to hire someone.
exampleSentence: Our team cannot take on any more projects this month.

definition: To move or learn at the same speed as others.
exampleSentence: It is hard to keep up with all the changes in technology.

definition: To remove or throw away something you do not want.
exampleSentence: We need to get rid of these old computers in the storage room.

definition: To contact someone again about something.
exampleSentence: I will follow up with the client by email tomorrow.

definition: To take someone or something to a place and leave them there.
exampleSentence: I can drop off the documents at your office on my way home.

definition: To confuse one thing or person with another.
exampleSentence: People often mix up the words "affect" and "effect" in English.

definition: To not include someone or something.
exampleSentence: Do not leave out any important details in your report.

definition: To draw a line through writing.
exampleSentence: If you make a mistake, simply cross out the wrong word.

definition: To consider something carefully before deciding.
exampleSentence: I need a few days to think over your job offer.

definition: To change and become something different.
exampleSentence: The small side project may turn into a successful business.

definition: To finally be in a place or situation you did not plan.
exampleSentence: If you do not use a map, you might end up in the wrong town.

definition: To give a short summary of the main points.
exampleSentence: At the end of the meeting, the manager will sum up the decisions.

definition: To make something happen faster.
exampleSentence: Closing unused apps in the background can speed up your phone.

definition: To keep time or money for a special purpose.
exampleSentence: Try to set aside some money every month for emergencies.

definition: To accept something annoying without complaining.
exampleSentence: I cannot put up with this slow internet connection any longer.

definition: To find something by chance.
exampleSentence: You may come across some old files while cleaning the server.

definition: To give a message or information to someone else.
exampleSentence: Could you pass on this message to your manager, please?

definition: To start doing something new, or to go to the next topic.
exampleSentence: Let us move on to the next item on the agenda.
